Chose: Pin MSW 2 in the install step, rather than support MSW 3

Anchored by tallow's as-built, Chose: Plain msw in the install step, undoing vellum's pin.

where projects/mock-control/README.md › mock-control › Setup › 1. Install file page

quote npm install -D @hypertheory-labs/mock-control msw@2 daisyui@5

Because (measured, then Claude, not asked): step 1's plain msw installed 3.0.3, now npm's latest. npm allowed it although the package's peer range is ^2.15.0; only npm ls called it invalid. Step 4's worker.start({ onUnhandledRequest }) then fails to compile. The Requirements already said MSW 2; the command didn't. Supporting MSW 3 was the other way out, and I didn't take it: the README's known limits were measured on 2.15, so a port is its own round with its own measurements, and it should be Jeff's call whether the class apps move.

Chose: daisyUI goes in the install step, and Requirements says how Tailwind arrives

where projects/mock-control/README.md › mock-control › Requirements file page

Because (measured): ng new --style=tailwind sets up Tailwind v4 but not daisyUI, and nothing in the README installed it; step 5's @plugin 'daisyui' assumed it.

Answered: Tailwind finds the panel's classes through the @source line

Answers the plan’s guess: held.

Answer (measured): held. In a fresh Angular 22 app with the package installed from npm pack of dist/mock-control, six classes only the panel uses (modal-end, tabs-border, badge-warning, btn-circle, tab-active, modal-box) are all in the built CSS with the line, and none are without it (121 KB against 28 KB). Repeated in a second fresh app following the fixed README. Not checked: how it looks in a browser. The CSS is the evidence; nobody has seen the panel render outside this workspace yet. This also answers pumice's guess, and clears what pumice said publishing waits on.

Answered: The README's setup works without knowing anything it doesn't say

Answers the plan’s guess: disproved.

Answer (measured): disproved, at step 1, and twice more. MSW 3 broke step 4, daisyUI was never installed, and the handler example didn't compile as written. Each is fixed in the README, and the fixed steps build in a second fresh app, in development and production. One thing I still had to know: ng new --style=tailwind. The README now says it, but whether a reader who doesn't know Angular's options needs more is a question only a reader can answer.
